title: Belt Drive Speed Calculator
description: Calculate the fan speed of three belt drives from the motor speed and the two sheave pitch diameters before the drive turns, then change the motor speed and either sheave to see the ratio, label and fan speed update.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the fan shaft speed of a belt drive from the motor speed and the two sheave pitch diameters, to within ±10 RPM.

rules: Fan speed rounded to the nearest 1 RPM; answers judged within ±10 RPM of the model value.
Ratio label: fan slower than motor (ratio < 1.000), fan same as motor (= 1.000), fan faster than motor (> 1.000).
assumptions: Pitch diameters; belt slip is not modeled.
limitations: Illustrative nominal motor speeds; real drives lose a little speed to belt slip.

sources: Standard belt-drive kinematics, ignoring belt slip
FanPedia, page 173 (a sheave change reaches the exact point of rating)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit a number, then watch the drive run; free exploration confronts sheave-size misconceptions
keyQuestions: What happens to fan speed when the fan sheave gets bigger?
Can a belt drive make the fan turn faster than the motor?
commonMisconceptions: A larger fan sheave makes the fan turn faster (it makes it turn slower).
A belt drive always slows the fan down (a larger motor sheave makes the fan faster than the motor).
Fan speed depends on the difference between the sheave sizes rather than their ratio.
assessmentOpportunities: 'Challenges correct: n of 3' running score; mastery is 3 of 3 on the first attempt.
